doc.title: Percy Humphrey Band: Percy Humphrey, Jim Robinson, Ernest Roubleau, Josiah Frazier Interview, 1972-02-29

chapter: Social life of old New Orleans
title: Honky tonks and cabarets
summary: Percy and Jim describe the honky tonks as cabarets with dancing and girls.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Cabarets, honky-tonks and the Storyville nightlife scene

blocks.x: Well, what about those honky tonks? Was it dangerous to go in them? No, no.

You know they used the slang, eh? That was my place. I'm getting out of the job round and then. Woo! Good time. That's all that. Good time. Dick, I know Dick. If you in your house, if the honky tonks was red, I bet you be in one every night. I know Dick, buddy. That's a cabaret. I know Dick. I know Dick.
It's a regular cabaret. It's a cabaret. It's a be dance. With the girls, man.
Be dance. Nice. Nice looking goods in there. Having a good time. Oh, but you man, that's whoop. And you kiss them, look.
Dick. Dick. Dick. Dick. It's nothing that now, Pop. I'll tell you. Oh, boy.
